question: Which of the following components of carrot does the human body convert into Vitamin A?
solution:
The correct answer is** __Beta carotene__**__.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Plants have a pigment called beta-carotene that gives them their colour.
 
• The Latin term for carrot is the source of the name beta-carotene.
 
• Many foods naturally contain** vitamin A, a fat-soluble vitamin. ** Vitamin A is essential for healthy reproduction, immunological function, growth and development, and vision. Vitamin A helps your heart, lungs, and other **organs to operate regularly. **
 
• **Fruits and vegetables that are yellow or orange** derive their vibrant colours from it. Additionally, foods like margarine are coloured with **beta-carotene.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Succinic acid is an alpha**, omega-dicarboxylic acid that is created when **butane's terminal methyl **groups are formally **oxidised to the equivalent carboxy group**. It is a metabolite that the citric acid cycle uses as an** intermediary.**
 
• The only type of **fat-soluble vitamin E **that is used by the human body is** alpha-tocopherol.** Its main job as an antioxidant is to scavenge loose electrons, often known as** "free radicals," **which can damage cells. 
 
• Almost **all living things need glutamic acid,** a -amino acid, in the production of proteins. **Humans can synthesise** it because it is not required for life. In the** nervous system of vertebrates**, it is also the excitatory neurotransmitter that is most prevalent.
